title: Rotations on the Coordinate Plane
text: In this lesson, you will build a convex polygon on a coordinate grid, choose its center of rotation, and explore how each vertex moves as you adjust the angle from −360° to 360°.

title: Rotations on the Coordinate Plane
text:
What to notice
A rotation turns every point through the same angle about a fixed center. In this tool, you choose the center \((h,k)\). Each vertex stays the same distance from that center, and the polygon keeps its side lengths and angle measures.
For a counterclockwise rotation by θ degrees around \((h,k)\), transform each point using:
x′ = h + (x − h) cos θ − (y − k) sin θ
y′ = k + (x − h) sin θ + (y − k) cos θ

title: Rotations on the Coordinate Plane
text:
Explore

Plot a triangle, then rotate it by 90°. Compare the original and image coordinates. What pattern do you notice?
Try 180°, −90°, and 270°. Which rotations produce the same image? Explain why.
Rotate your polygon by 360° and −360°. What happens to each vertex?
Predict the image of one vertex before moving the slider, then use the graph to check your prediction.

title: Rotations on the Coordinate Plane
text:
Learning goals

Plot and identify vertices of a polygon on the coordinate plane.
Describe and model a rotation by its angle and center.
Compare coordinates before and after a rotation and explain how the transformation preserves distance and angle measure.

title: Welcome!
text:
Welcome to my teaching website! This is a space where I share my teaching philosophy, educational resources, classroom activities, and reflections on my development as an educator.
My goal is to create meaningful learning experiences that encourage students to explore ideas, ask questions, make connections, and develop confidence in their mathematical abilities. I hope this website provides a glimpse into my approach to teaching and my commitment to helping every student learn.

title: Welcome!
text:
Teaching Philosophy
I believe students develop a lasting understanding of mathematics when they actively explore ideas and make connections, rather than simply receive answers or memorize procedures. I want students to feel comfortable asking questions, sharing their thinking, making mistakes, and building models as they work toward their own understanding. Visualization, discussion, hands-on activities, and mathematical construction can each offer a different way into an idea.
My approach also needs to be flexible. I aim to respond to students’ interests, questions, and needs while providing the guidance and structure that keep learning focused. I see reflection as part of that work: revising lessons, improving explanations, addressing misconceptions, and learning from mistakes help me find better ways to support students.

title: Welcome!
text:
My Role as a Teacher
My role is to create these connections while providing enough structure and guidance to keep students moving toward meaningful understanding. At the same time, I recognize that effective teaching requires constant reflection. I want to hold myself to high standards by carefully revising my lessons, thinking about the language I use, responding to students’ misconceptions, and learning from my mistakes. I believe becoming a better teacher is a continuous process, and through consistency, preparation, and a willingness to learn alongside my students, I hope to create a classroom where students feel confident exploring mathematics and developing their own understanding.
